strengths_deep_dive: While the foundation faces operational limitations, its core spending remains focused on direct aid. In FY2024, the organization spent <cite id="2">95.4% of its expenses on program execution</cite>, sending <cite id="2">$2,612,196 in domestic grants</cite> to support the A S Edhi Foundation's direct services in Pakistan. Furthermore, the charity reports a <cite id="3">fundraising efficiency of $0.00 per $1 raised</cite>, meaning it does not divert donor funds toward third-party fundraising companies.
rich_narrative.summary: The Abdul Sattar Edhi International Foundation Inc. operates as a US-based fundraising arm supporting relief efforts in Pakistan, reporting <cite id="2">Total Revenue of $5,242,874 in FY2024</cite>. The organization directs the vast majority of its financial output toward aid, maintaining a <cite id="2">Program expense ratio of 95.4%</cite>. However, significant financial management issues severely limit its effectiveness. Most critically, the foundation holds <cite id="3">120.5 months of operating reserves</cite> in cash and liquid assets. Holding over ten years of expenses in reserve is a major concern for a relief charity, as it indicates that donations—including obligatory religious giving—are accumulating in bank accounts rather than reaching impoverished populations in a timely manner. Additionally, revenue declined in FY2024 from <cite id="2">$5,752,945 in FY2023 to $5,242,874</cite>.
